Why Facebook shows “AI info” on your photo or video — and how to avoid it

Posted a real photo with a small AI retouch and Facebook tagged it “AI info”? Facebook uses the same system as Instagram and Threads: it reads metadata inside the file. Here is how it works and what you can do.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 4 min read
Short answer: Facebook shows “AI info” when the file carries metadata (C2PA Content Credentials or IPTC fields) saying it was created or edited with AI, or when you add the AI label yourself while posting. To avoid a label caused by metadata, clean the file before uploading: drop it into IA Cleaner, download the clean copy and post that one. On a post that is already up it usually can’t be removed — you have to post it again.

What triggers the label on Facebook

  • C2PA Content Credentials written by ChatGPT, Adobe Firefly, Photoshop’s generative features, Galaxy AI and other tools.
  • IPTC / XMP DigitalSourceType values that mean “generated by AI” or “edited with AI”.
  • Your own choice: the AI label you can switch on when you create a post or reel.

Meta applies the same system to Instagram and Threads, so a file that gets the label on one usually gets it on the others.

Clean the file before posting

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images (or Video for a reel).
  2. Drop the photo or video. The report shows every metadata block and flags AI-related ones.
  3. Download the clean copy and upload that one to Facebook.

What this won’t change

  • A label you added yourself, or one Meta applies because of its own detection.
  • Invisible watermarks inside the pixels, such as SynthID.
  • Meta’s rules: realistic AI-generated content should be disclosed. Cleaning metadata is for privacy and for wrong labels on real photos, not for hiding synthetic media.

Also see the Instagram guide, which works the same way.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) it identifies and removes GPS location, camera and phone model, dates, editing apps, XMP and IPTC data, C2PA Content Credentials and embedded AI prompts. Pixels and colour profile stay the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
